thread:
maria: Quick thread 1: Delegated cancel semantics + a tiny preflight to help the edge decide about fallbacks. Weve been handling client cancels as opaque EOFs which makes streaming side-effects awkward. Proposal: explicit capability exchange so edge can act deterministically.
ryan: +1. We need 3 pragmatic modes I can think of: `abort` (immediate stop), `drain` (let upstream finish current commit window), and `ack` (edge acknowledges cancel and promises final status later).
theo: Agree. Important: `drain` requires a bounded commit window or we blow up concurrency. Must be a route-configured cap and tenant quota.
jess: Observability: we must tag traces/metrics with why fallback happened: `reason=client_cancel|upstream_err|edge_forced`. Also annotate spans with `cancel_mode` and `commit_window_ms`.
maria: Draft header surface: `x-rw-cancel-behavior: abort|drain|ack`, `x-rw-fallback-policy: none|attempt|defer`, `x-rw-commit-window-ms: <int>`. Upstream advertises `x-rw-supports-retry: yes|no|partial` during a preflight handshake. Edge caches preflight per-route.
ryan: For streaming (HTTP chunked / gRPC / WS) we need that handshake before any side-effectful tokens emit. Idea: do a cheap OPTIONS /_edge_cap that returns the headers. If `supports-retry=no` edge never attempts fallback.
theo: Operational limits: add `max_commit_window_ms` to route schema and a tenant-wide `drain_window_budget` counter. If budget exhausted, edge downgrades `drain` -> `abort` and emits `downgraded=true` in logs.
jess: Metrics checklist: `edge.cancel.behavior.{abort,drain,ack}.count`, `edge.fallback.attempts`, `edge.fallback.reason`, `edge.downgrade.count`. Traces: a light span at cancel time with attributes `{cancel_mode, initial_preflight_support, downgraded}`.
maria: Sequence example:
```
Client -> Edge: POST /v1/generate (body)
Edge -> Route Cache: lookup route config
Edge -> Upstream (preflight): OPTIONS /_edge_cap -> returns headers above
Edge -> Upstream: open streaming POST with `x-rw-cancel-behavior` set by route or client
Client cancels -> Edge sees cancel
  - if abort -> drop connection to upstream immediately
  - if drain -> send `x-rw-signal: cancel-drain` to upstream and start commit timer
  - if ack -> close client stream, return 202 ack, continue to finish and send final webhook/notification when done
If upstream signals `support/retry=yes` and route fallback_policy=attempt -> edge may call fallback endpoint or hedged replica
```
maria: Edge should enforce that client-supplied headers cannot escalate privileges. Only route-enabled modes are honored and preflight is authoritative.
ryan: Security/abuse: reject client-requested commit windows > route max. Also rate-limit ack-mode per-tenant to avoid holding resources.
theo: Implementation notes: preflight cached per route+model+tenant key, TTL like 5m. Preflight should be light-weight (no heavy model init). Also, make drain timer configurable with a hard upper-bound enforced in edge process.
jess: Alerting: `forced_drain_count` (drain expired and we forced abort) and `fallback_duplicate_tokens` (heuristic duplicate output observed). Add runbook for `forced_drain > 1%` per-route.
maria: Who takes ownership? @ryan spike preflight + header contract. @theo add route schema knobs and tenant quotas. @jess write metrics + runbook. I'll coordinate a short API doc for SDKs so devs understand ack/drain semantics.
ryan: I'll put up a small proto repo under `edge/preflight` and link a draft by EOW.
theo: I'll add schema PR for `max_commit_window_ms` & `drain_budget` in route config.
jess: I'll stub dashboards/alerts in observability and sync with SRE.
